doc: Round 39 (campaign 14): one cross-language conformance corpus. Each verdict vector is a real Core
verdict from this directory (`base`), changed by `raw_replace` (exact text replacements on the committed
file, each matching once) and then `edits` (set / delete / push at a JSON path). Every implementation
reads the result and must give the outcome `expect` names for it:
rust  - the Core's own type and rule: serde_json into VerificationResult, then is_executable()
guard - the agent guard's ResidualPolicy (default, and accepting every acceptable code) on the
Outcomes: executable | not_executable | unreadable; for the guard signs | refuses. A client may be
STRICTER than the Core's rule (a `note` says why) and never looser: every test also asserts that
nothing a client calls executable is not executable to the Core's rule.
`content_hash` vectors pin the framed v2 instruction bind key; `transaction_digest` vectors pin
scope.transaction_sha256 (signature slots zeroed). `expect: null` means only that every
implementation computes the same value, and `differs_from` that it differs from the named vector.
